fixes.explanation: Sabbath and New Moon, friend. The Lord GOD says the gate stays shut during the six days of work, “…but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.” So the work week keeps it closed, and those two days are when it opens.
The priests, friend. The prince stands by the gatepost, and the priests are the ones who sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings. Those offerings are his, but the sacrificing is theirs.
Prophets don't show up in this verse, friend. It's the priests who sacrifice the prince's burnt offerings and peace offerings. The prince stands by the gatepost while they do it.
Nice try, friend, but there's no speech in this verse. The text says he bows in worship at the threshold of the gate and then departs. No reading, just a bow.
Nobles aren't named here. The text says the people of the land are also to bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway. That's on the Sabbaths and New Moons.

East gate? I love the confidence, friend, but this verse only talks about the north and south gates. A worshiper who enters by the north gate must go out by the south gate. No one is to return through the gate by which he entered, so no turning around.

I get the doubt, friend, but this one is true. The text says that when the prince makes a freewill offering, the gate facing east must be opened for him. After he goes out, the gate must be closed. So it opens for him and shuts behind him.

Brothers? Good guess, friend, but they aren't in this verse. The text says the gift to a son will belong to his descendants. It becomes their property by inheritance, so it stays down the family line.
Priests getting a servant's gift? I see the thinking, friend, but the text doesn't send it there. A gift to a servant belongs to that servant until the year of freedom. Then it reverts to the prince.

No gatekeepers in this spot, friend. The man says it's where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering. It's also where they bake the grain offering, so it's a kitchen, not a bunkhouse.

True, friend. The man says the priests cook those offerings there “…so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.” So the cooking happens in the holy chambers. The outer court is kept clear of it.

It's actually true, friend. The man says the priests boil and bake there “…so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.” So the cooking spot sits at the far western end of the priests' holy chambers, and the outer court stays out of it. That's the reason the text gives.
